Seamless days (Nov 3): the time column stays put while the days scroll sideways under it, so a day header scrolled to the far left slides under the time column's top cell. By design; the day is reachable by scrolling.
The auto-scheduler is a floating window over the calendar by design (owner, Nov 3): it moves by its title, resizes and minimizes to a chip, so what it covers can always be uncovered.
The perched owl sits at the screen's bottom-left on phones; a tap sends it to another perch. It covered the last calendar card's XP in the day view only when scrolled to the very bottom.

The auto-scheduler is a floating window (moves, resizes, minimizes); at its default spot on a phone its last row's × can sit under the always-there feedback button. Moving or shrinking the window uncovers it (Nov 6).
The minimized packing window is a floating chip (like the language and auto-scheduler chips): it stays where the window was and floats over the page by design; drag it anywhere, tap to open.

The offline flow cuts the connection on purpose (Nov 7): the browser logs the requests it couldn't make (prefetches, the server-side reload). The flow itself fails if the screens don't open or the changes don't sync.
The offline pill's short explanation (opened by tapping the pill) floats over the page header for as long as it's open; tapping the pill again closes it. By design (no popup screen).

Packing lists (owner, Nov 7, like Listry): a packed item waits about a second with its tick showing, then glides to the bottom of its section. By design; Settings › Packed things › Stay put keeps it in place.

Prioritize cards (Nov 10): swiping a card left slides it partly out of the deck on purpose to uncover its Snooze button (like SwipeReveal on Today's cards); the deck clips it sideways. Tapping × or the card brings it back whole.
